editorial:
Imagine being pushed to your absolute limit at a world-class dance school where the pressure is so high that people actually start dying. You get to follow Inspector Michel Eparvier as he tries to figure out why these young women are dropping dead. The vibe is super tense because you see the teacher, Wolf, pushing these girls past their breaking point. He makes them repeat the same movements for hours, turning a beautiful art into something that feels like a nightmare. It feels like a mix of a crime show and a psychological drama, making you wonder if the deaths are just accidents or something way more sinister.

What really works here is how the movie builds up the stress of the training. The acting is solid, and the mystery keeps you guessing until the end. While the pacing starts a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. If you enjoy movies about dark secrets in high-pressure environments, you will love this one. You should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture quality, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. If you are a big collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great call.
endingExplained: In the end, it turns out that Wolf was intentionally pushing the students to death to achieve a kind of twisted perfection. The twist reveals that the physical exhaustion was a cover for his obsession with control. Inspector Eparvier finally gathers enough evidence to prove that the deaths weren't just accidents. Wolf is caught, and the cycle of abuse at the school finally stops, leaving the surviving students to recover from the trauma.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and stories about obsessed teachers.
